observed_gap: Qwen tool-executor keeps workspace in one process-global mutable variable. initWorkspace() changes that variable for every later file/shell tool call in the process.

A future Notion->Qwen adapter may run two independent delegated children concurrently. If they target different projects and select their workspaces per child, child B can switch the global workspace after child A has started but before A reaches a tool call. A's tool then resolves inside B's project.
The current provider-neutral Notion DelegationRequest/DelegationContext contains task/parent/conversation/objective/max-turns but no stable workspace/project identity.

Qwen persisted coding-subagent batch signature covers task prompt/skill names plus mode/model/session/settings/owner-prompt hash, but not a stable workspace identity. Therefore the same deterministic delegated task/batch/session identity can validate across two logical projects unless the future adapter adds an extra contract field.

minimal_safe_contract.delegation_workspace_identity: The parent/agent layer supplies a stable opaque logical workspace/project identity. Do not use a mutable checkout fingerprint and do not expose a local absolute path to provider-visible prompts.
minimal_safe_contract.qwen_persisted_signature: Include only SHA-256(workspace identity) in the Qwen persisted execution signature. Reusing a batch id for a different workspace must fail with signature mismatch before any tool execution or prior-result resume.
minimal_safe_contract.runtime_isolation: Long-term: bind a tool executor/workspace immutably to each delegated Qwen session instead of one process-global workspace. Safe interim adapter: serialize the whole initWorkspace + coding-subagent lifetime behind one cross-workspace process lock, never just the individual tool call.
minimal_safe_contract.concurrency_rule: Concurrent Qwen delegated children are allowed only when their tool executors have independent immutable workspace bindings. Otherwise fail closed or serialize them.
minimal_safe_contract.restart_rule: The stable workspace identity must survive restart and relocation of the same logical project; absolute filesystem path alone is not a sufficient identity.

why_this_is_integration_specific: Qwen's current single-workspace process can be valid in isolation, and Notion's provider-neutral delegation can be valid before a Qwen adapter exists. The cross-project isolation failure appears when Notion's parallel child lifecycle is connected to Qwen's process-global tool workspace and deterministic persisted subagent state.
limits: No Qwen or Notion product source was rewritten.
No CircleCI, GitHub Actions, Cloudflare or other hosted CI was started.
No production, real account data or secrets touched.
